lines: A digital copy of Mannequins' Cold Mac: a crossfader, an OR and AND pair, a rectifier, an envelope follower, a wavefolder, an integrator and a mixer, tied together by normalling and one big knob
Feeds the FADE, OR2, AND2 and SLOPE inputs while nothing is patched to them, as 0 to 1 for FADE and as -5V to 5V for the other three, and sets the level of the CHEESE mixer
Adds to the MACRO knob, 10V covering its whole travel for the FADE normalling, and adds volt for volt to the -5V to 5V that knob sends to OR2, AND2 and SLOPE; both totals are clamped
Sets the crossfade, -5V putting the LEFT input on the LEFT output and 5V putting it on the RIGHT output; with nothing patched the MACRO knob does this over its own travel
LEFT input — one end of the crossfade, and one of the six signals in the CHEESE mixer; with nothing patched it reads -5V
Adds volt for volt to both the LEFT and RIGHT outputs after the crossfade, before those outputs are clamped to -5V and 5V
RIGHT input — the other end of the crossfade, and one of the six signals in the CHEESE mixer; with nothing patched it reads 5V
The second signal into the OR comparison; with nothing patched the MACRO knob supplies it as -5V to 5V
The first signal into the OR comparison, which also feeds the AND1 input and the CHEESE mixer; with nothing patched it reads 0V
The second signal into the AND comparison; with nothing patched the MACRO knob supplies it as -5V to 5V
The first signal into the AND comparison, and one of the six signals in the CHEESE mixer; with nothing patched the OR1 input supplies it
SLOPE input — rectified for the SLOPE output and followed for the FOLLOW output, and it also feeds CREASE and the CHEESE mixer; the MACRO knob supplies it unpatched
CREASE input — folded for the CREASE output and integrated for the LOCATION output, and one of the six in the CHEESE mixer; the SLOPE input supplies it unpatched
LEFT output — the crossfade, carrying the LEFT input with FADE at -5V and the RIGHT input with FADE at 5V, plus OFFSET, clamped to -5V and 5V
RIGHT output — the other side of the crossfade, carrying the RIGHT input with FADE at -5V and the LEFT input with FADE at 5V, plus OFFSET, clamped to -5V and 5V
Whichever of OR1 and OR2 is the higher voltage at that moment, clamped to -5V and 5V
Whichever of AND1 and AND2 is the lower voltage at that moment, clamped to -5V and 5V
SLOPE output — the SLOPE input rectified, so a negative voltage comes out positive, reading 0V to 5V
The rectified SLOPE input through a one-pole lowpass at 5Hz and multiplied by 1.5, an envelope follower reading 0V to 10V
CREASE output — the CREASE input folded: 5V is taken off a positive voltage and added to a negative one, so 0V comes out as -5V and 5V comes out as 0V
The CREASE input added up over time, an integrator that climbs while CREASE is positive and falls while it is negative, and stops at -5V and 5V
The LEFT, RIGHT, OR1, AND1, SLOPE and CREASE inputs mixed with the DC taken out of each, scaled by the MACRO knob and soft clipped, approaching 10V
Note — every jack is normalled from another one, so the module puts out voltage with nothing patched at all: turning MACRO alone moves the OR, AND, SLOPE, FOLLOW, CREASE and LOCATION outputs.
Note — the CHEESE mixer takes the inputs and not the outputs: LEFT and RIGHT before the crossfade, OR1 and AND1 rather than the OR and AND results, and SLOPE and CREASE before rectifying and folding.
Note — the LOCATION integrator adds the CREASE voltage once per sample without allowing for the sample rate, so it travels twice as fast at 96kHz as at 48kHz.
Note — the module is monophonic: every jack reads or writes one channel.
Menu — Default Location Speed — makes the LOCATION integrator add the CREASE voltage divided by 25000 each sample, and is the setting a new module takes
Menu — Glacial Location Speed — makes the LOCATION integrator add the CREASE voltage divided by 300000 each sample, the slowest of the six
Menu — Sluggish Location Speed — makes the LOCATION integrator add the CREASE voltage divided by 115200 each sample
Menu — Slowish Location Speed — makes the LOCATION integrator add the CREASE voltage divided by 50000 each sample
Menu — Quickish Location Speed — makes the LOCATION integrator add the CREASE voltage divided by 12500 each sample
Menu — Snappy Location Speed — makes the LOCATION integrator add the CREASE voltage divided by 6250 each sample, the fastest of the six

chilly_cheese.notes:
Written against commit cff07c4, the first commit whose plugin.json carries 2.0.7; nothing under src or res has changed between it and the repository head, so the source read is the source that shipped.

The MACRO knob has two forms in the code and they normal different jacks: the raw 0 to 1 value normals FADE and sets the CHEESE mixer level, and the same value stretched to -5V to 5V (src/chilly_cheese.cpp:134) normals OR2, AND2 and SLOPE. The MACRO CV jack is added to both, a tenth of it to the first and all of it to the second (:139-142).

The manual says the LOCATION speed menu offers five choices; the menu builds six (src/chilly_cheese.cpp:283-290), and the manual's own statement that Default sits halfway between Slowish and Quickish holds, since 25000 is the geometric middle of 50000 and 12500.

The integrator is not compensated for sample rate: :216 adds crease times a fixed constant once per process call, so the LOCATION output moves at a rate proportional to the sample rate. Everything else in the module is sample-rate aware through the 5Hz follower at :129.

The OFFSET jack is read with plain getVoltage at :161 rather than behind an isConnected test, so it contributes 0V rather than being normalled to anything; the panel marks the other macro-normalled jacks with an M bubble and leaves OFFSET unmarked, which matches.

No control is polyphonic. Every read is getVoltage with no channel argument and every write is setVoltage with no channel argument, and nothing calls setChannels.
